purpose: Summative evidence for B2.6 (division as equal sharing) and B2.1 (multiplication-division relationship).
student_learning_goal: I can share up to 12 items fairly between 2, 3, 4, or 6 friends, and write the division equation.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can share up to 12 items fairly between 2, 3, 4, or 6 friends, and write the division equation.
header.character_watermark: Mae, Dan, and Buddy together in the top-right corner. Small (~1.5in tall combined).

parts.student_instructions: Share each collection of cookies fairly. Draw the share. Write the division equation.
parts.visual_layout: Top of the page. Three sharing scenes stacked.

image_placeholders.description: Three sharing scenes in B&W line-art, stacked vertically. Each scene ~7in × 1.8in. Scene A: 12 cookies, 3 plates. Scene B: 12 cookies, 4 plates. Scene C: 12 cookies, 6 plates. Each plate ~1.2in diameter.
image_placeholders.placement: Top of the page; three scenes stacked.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS05_P1_THREE_SHARES: keywords (cookies, share) name what the scenes show.

parts.answer_key: Scene A: 4 cookies on each plate; 12 ÷ 3 = 4. Scene B: 3 cookies on each plate; 12 ÷ 4 = 3. Scene C: 2 cookies on each plate; 12 ÷ 6 = 2.

parts.student_instructions: Each triangle has 3 numbers. Write all 4 facts: 2 multiplications + 2 divisions.
parts.visual_layout: Middle. Three fact-family triangles in a row.

image_placeholders.description: Three fact-family triangles in B&W line-art, in a row. Each ~1.8in tall with 3 numbers at the corners. Numbers: T1 (3, 4, 12); T2 (2, 6, 12); T3 (4, 5, 20). Below each triangle, four equation lines.
image_placeholders.placement: Middle of the page; three triangles in a row.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS05_P2_THREE_TRIANGLES: keywords (triangle, facts) name what the triangles show.

parts.student_instructions: Read each short story. Label MULTIPLY (×) or DIVIDE (÷). Write the equation.
parts.visual_layout: Lower-middle. Six story boxes in a 2x3 grid.

image_placeholders.description: Six short story boxes in B&W line-art, 2-row × 3-column grid. Each box ~2.2in × 1.8in. Pre-filled stories: S1 'Mae has 4 baskets of 3 kittens. How many altogether?'; S2 '12 cookies shared by 4 friends. How many each?'; S3 '5 boxes of 6 crayons each. How many crayons total?'; S4 '12 stickers shared by 3 kids. How many each?'; S5 '6 plates of 2 muffins. How many muffins?'; S6 '8 marbles shared by 2 friends. How many each?'. Below each story, an × / ÷ bubble and an equation line.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS05_P3_SIX_STORIES: keywords (story) name what the boxes ask for.

parts.student_instructions: Mae and Dan have 12 paper kittens. How many DIFFERENT ways can they share them fairly between friends? List all the ways.
parts.visual_layout: Bottom of the page. A blank box with thinking-bubble icon.

image_placeholders.description: A blank rectangular drawing box in B&W line-art, ~7in × 2.5in, with light-grey solid outline. Mae and Dan thinking-bubble icons in the top-right corner.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS05_P4_WAYS_BOX: keywords (share, ways) name what the box asks for.

parts.answer_key: 12 has these factors: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. So fair-share ways are: 12÷1 (one friend gets all 12), 12÷2 (6 each for 2 friends), 12÷3 (4 each), 12÷4 (3 each), 12÷6 (2 each), 12÷12 (1 each for 12 friends). Six ways total.

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, write your own fact-family triangle with three numbers between 2 and 10. Then write all 4 facts.
teacher_notes: Lesson 5 capstone summative worksheet. Hand out at the end of the Action phase. Use Parts 1-4 as summative evidence for B2.6 + B2.1. Watch for: (a) Part 1 children who don't deal fairly (uneven shares) — flag for the deal-fairly reteach; (b) Part 2 children who only write 2 facts per triangle (missing the divisions) — flag for fact-family reteach; (c) Part 4 children who list only 2-3 ways — coaching opportunity for systematic listing of factors.
